messages:
lina_support: FYI — acme-inc is seeing intermittent 502/504 spikes hitting our hosted API since ~08:30 UTC. They say it mostly affects streaming/chat endpoints and happens ~every few minutes. Attaching sample trace and a short repro next.

miguel_sre: Can you drop a sample x-request-id / trace id and a curl repro so we can correlate logs?

lina_support: sample request id `req=01a2b3c4` and trace `trace=acme-7788`. Customer curl they used: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --http2 https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/chat -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'``` Response intermittently returns 502 with body `{"error":"UpstreamServiceError"}`. Response headers we see: `server: envoy`, `x-request-id: 01a2b3c4`, `via: 1.1 redwood-edge`

oncall-bot: [alert] ingress-gateway: 502 rate increased from 0.2% to 4.5% over last 10m for cluster: hostedapi-edge (alert-id: ag-502-spike-1764)

miguel_sre: thanks. I pulled logs for `req=01a2b3c4` (sensitive parts redacted). Key lines: ```[2026-03-01T08:31:12Z] ingress-gateway info incoming request req=01a2b3c4 route=/v1/chat
[2026-03-01T08:31:42Z] envoy warning upstream reset: remote rst stream_id=1 req=01a2b3c4
[2026-03-01T08:31:42Z] ingress-gateway error response 502 req=01a2b3c4 backend=upstream-chat-1
``` Observed pattern: upstream connection being reset ~30s after request start.

kevin_platform: this smells like a keepalive/idle timeout mismatch between the LB and our upstreams or an auth-proxy (frontdoor) that closes long-lived streams. Quick checks: are we seeing `tcp_close` counters on the upstream pool and any GOAWAYs from the LB? Miguel can you check Envoy stats for `upstream_cx_closed` / `upstream_cx_rx_bytes_total`?

miguel_sre: checked metrics dashboard for ingress-gateway: `upstream_cx_closed_with_error` spiked matching 502 window. Also seeing `http2.rx_reset` increments. No obvious increase in backend CPU/memory.

lina_support: customer says it affects streaming more (longer lived), while short (non-stream) requests mostly fine. They reproduced by keeping connection idle for ~25-35s and then sending payload = 502.

miguel_sre: repro steps I ran locally (works): ```# repro (http2) curl --http2 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -v https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/chat -d @payload.json``` then wait ~30s, send the next chunk. I saw reset from remote. On tcpdump we see FIN from upstream side shortly before envoy logged reset.

kevin_platform: probable root cause: heartbeat/keepalive offset — frontdoor LB is closing idle connection earlier (30s) while upstream/Envoy expects longer. For streaming requests that hold the connection idle between chunks, the LB's idle close turns into upstream reset -> 502. Short term mitigation: lower our client-side idle window by sending periodic tiny pings or enable `connection: keep-alive` with a shorter keepalive on the client; long term we need to align idle timeouts or enable TCP keepalive on the LB->envoy path.

miguel_sre: agreed. Short-term patch: enable per-route `idle_timeout: 60s` on the envoy route for streaming endpoints to tolerate LB flaps, and add a tiny persistent ping every 20s from edge->upstream. I'll open a canary config.

lina_support: I told the customer a temporary workaround: add periodic small heartbeats from client if they can. They can also retry on 502. Customer is okay with workaround for now but asked for ETA.

kevin_platform: created ENG-4021 to track: "ingress keepalive/idle-timeout misalignment causing streaming 502s". Owner: @miguel_sre. Target: canary config in 2 hours, full rollout after monitoring for 30m.

miguel_sre: putting up canary now -> route patch + metrics alert tweak. Will post canary id when done.

lina_support: noted, I updated the customer (ACME-12345) with the workaround and ETA. I'll attach trace req `01a2b3c4` to the ticket. :thumbsup:

kevin_platform: follow-ups: 1) add synthetic test that keeps stream idle for 40s and asserts no 502, 2) update runbook with troubleshooting steps + canonical curl repro, 3) create dashboard panel for `http2.rx_reset` on ingress-gateway.

miguel_sre: canary rolled: patch id `canary-8832`. Early numbers: 502 rate for canary nodes dropped from 4.5% -> 0.4% within 12m. Continuing to observe.

lina_support: thanks team — I'll keep the customer posted and close this thread once ENG-4021 reaches QA/rollout.
